entry.title: An authored scenario can claim that a consumer halted an ordered scan
entry.summary: `halts_after: <n>` lets an authored scenario require a consumer to stop an ordered scan after n rows. The target reports rows produced and whether the consumer ended the read. Targets without incremental reads report `unsupported`. This adds a claim to `ess-conformance/4`.

entry.title: A specification's scenarios can be played in a browser
entry.summary: `ess verify conform web` emits a browser page that walks authored scenarios, showing actors, state, selected views, and declared consequences. It replays model-determined behavior without executing an implementation, so authors can inspect a specification before filling its obligations.

entry.title: A specification carries the scenarios an author wrote, not only the ones it obliges
entry.summary: Authors can declare modelled instances, command timelines, and expectations in `ess-scenario/1`. These scenarios compile into `ess-conformance/2` with identities distinct from synthesized suites. Twenty-seven refusals check their names against the model. Included in the published 0.16.0 release.

entry.title: An authored scenario can claim a length of time, and a target has to answer for it
entry.summary: Authored scenarios gain `mark:` and `elapsed:` with `not_before`, `within`, and `quiet` bounds. The suite states a duration and its anchor; the target reports an observed or advanced clock. Targets without clock support report `unsupported`. The claims use `ess-conformance/3`.

entry.title: A component can declare a command-line surface, and ESS synthesizes its parser
entry.summary: `reached_by: command_line` and a `cli:` block state that a component's callers are people at a terminal and where each command sits in the tree. `ess generate synthesize --target clap` emits the parser, the handler obligations and the completion scripts from that declaration.

entry.title: ESS becomes a standalone executable specification toolchain
entry.summary: ESS 0.1.0 extracts system modeling, schema contracts, generators, and conformance into an independent repository with no AEP dependency.
